title: Introduction to Laboratory Chemistry - Chemistry - Preparation of Solutions
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: You need to prepare $250\ \text{mL}$ of a $2.0\ \text{M}$ ​$\text{NaCl}$ solution. How many moles of $\text{NaCl}$ are required?
questions.explain:
Using the molarity formula $M = \frac{\text{moles}}{\text{liters}}$:
$$\text{moles} = M \times V = 2.0\ \text{mol/L} \times 0.250\ \text{L} = 0.50\ \text{moles}$$

questions.q: When diluting a concentrated acid to prepare a standard solution, what is the crucial safety rule?
options: Always add water to the acid.
Always add the acid to the water.
Mix the acid and water rapidly in a sealed container.
questions.explain: **Add Acid to Water (AA)**. Adding water to concentrated acid can cause the water to boil instantly due to the high heat of hydration, potentially splashing acid out. Adding acid slowly to a larger volume of water dissipates the heat safely.
